findings.requirement: Stored sessions tolerate missing or damaged browser state.
findings.behavior: A damaged non-JSON value in localStorage causes JSON.parse to throw a SyntaxError instead of returning a recoverable empty or invalid-session result.
findings.impact: Users with corrupted or legacy browser state can be blocked from loading the application or restoring a session until storage is manually cleared.
findings.reproduction: Set localStorage.session to "damaged", then call loadSession(). The added line throws SyntaxError: Unexpected token instead of tolerating the stored state. A missing key happens to parse as null through coercion, but damaged state still violates the rule.
findings.recommendation: Restore a tolerant parsing boundary: read the nullable value, return an empty-session result when absent, and catch or validate malformed JSON before passing it through session-shape validation. Add a regression test that fails before and passes after for both a missing key and malformed stored JSON.

findings.requirement: Approval requires an approver role and complete evidence; note text is not authorization.
findings.behavior: Approval is granted solely when untrusted note text contains "approved", without checking the user's approver role or request.evidenceComplete.
findings.impact: Any user able to supply note text can approve a request with incomplete evidence, bypassing both authorization and required evidence controls.
findings.reproduction: Call canApprove({ roles: [] }, { evidenceComplete: false, note: "approved" }). The added implementation returns true, although the caller has no approver role and the evidence is incomplete.
findings.recommendation: Require both user.roles.includes("approver") and request.evidenceComplete; treat note text only as descriptive data. Add regression tests proving non-approvers and incomplete-evidence requests remain denied even when their note contains "approved", while an approver with complete evidence is allowed.
